= Manual of style adapted for Malagasy Wikipedia translation =

== Scope, sources, and precedence ==
This is mgwiki-editor's local operational adaptation, not an official policy
adopted by the Malagasy Wikipedia community and not a full translation of every
English MoS subpage. Read it together with SKILL.md and words-to-watch.wiki.

Adapted from Wikipedia contributors, [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style&oldid=1381654087 Wikipedia:Manual of Style, revision 1381654087],
consulted 3 November 2026, and
[https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch&oldid=1382059772 Words to watch, revision 1382059772].
The linked revision histories identify contributing authors. Source text is
available under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0; this adaptation of
that material is shared under the same license. It condenses and localizes the
English guidance and adds the user's Malagasy project conventions.

Explicit Malagasy rules in SKILL.md control apostrophe spacing, name order,
foreign-word italics, acronym glosses, agency translations, and italic paper
titles. Do not import English possessive grammar, national English spelling
preferences, English title case, or English-specific plural rules into Malagasy.
Verified community policy and factual/quotation accuracy remain constraints;
record a genuine conflict instead of inventing a consensus or silently erasing it.

Use these saved references offline. Their links provide provenance, not standing
authorization to open other pages. Do not fetch the MoS or its subpages for each
article. No external research, resource loading, or on-wiki edits are authorized
merely by reading this manual.

== Existing style, clarity, and neutral voice ==
* Use a consistent, clear, concise encyclopedic style accessible to a general
  Malagasy reader. Natural Malagasy grammar takes priority over source syntax.
* Retain an existing acceptable style when several styles are permitted. Do not
  churn optional punctuation, citation styles or layout, or edit-war over style.
  The explicit project conventions apply to the new Malagasy sandbox draft,
  not as permission for mass mainspace corrections.
* Use neutral third-person exposition, not instructions, rhetorical questions,
  promotional claims, first-person editorial commentary, or appeals to readers.
* Preserve qualifications, evidential strength, negation, causation versus
  correlation, chronology and source attribution. Neither embellish nor conceal.
* Explain necessary technical vocabulary in clear Malagasy. Prefer a precise
  descriptive explanation to an unverified technical coinage. Retained foreign
  terms are italicized, including parenthetical originals.
* Respect people's documented names and identities. Do not infer gender from a
  name, import unnecessary gender distinctions from English, expose private
  former names, or add personal details unsupported by the source.

== Article titles, layout, and headings ==
* Choose a recognizable, natural, precise, concise Malagasy topic title. Preserve
  established proper-name spelling. Do not add a sentence-ending punctuation
  mark unless it is genuinely part of a name/title.
* Start with an unheaded lead defining the subject and summarizing the supported
  body. Bold the subject's name at first mention; use no extra decorative bold.
* Follow the lead with coherent sections rather than a mechanical source outline.
  Keep sourced existing Malagasy contributions when merging.
* Use descriptive sentence-case headings: == Tantara ==, then === ... === without
  skipping levels. No redundant topic name in every heading, numbered headings,
  rhetorical questions, pseudo-headings made from bold or list markup, links,
  footnotes, images, or formula markup inside a section heading.
* Keep headings unique, on separate lines, with a preceding blank line. Preserve
  necessary existing section anchors when changing a heading, using valid local
  markup, not an assumed English template.
* After the body, order suitable appendices consistently: the subject's works,
  related articles, notes/references, selective further reading, external links.
  Distinguish works by the subject from works used as references.
* Only use locally verified templates/parameters. Do not copy English language-
  variety templates, short descriptions, maintenance banners, infoboxes, authority
  control, or category-producing templates blindly. Sandbox categories stay
  inert; no mainspace edits, redirect creation or Wikidata changes.

== Capitalization and typography ==
* Prefer sentence case in headings and ordinary Malagasy prose. Capitalize
  actual proper names according to established usage, not all important words.
* Preserve the original spelling, diacritics, internal word order, and meaningful
  capitalization of foreign names and titles. Do not impose English title case
  on a Malagasy translation or another language's title.
* Distinguish a specific named institution, office, religion or region from a
  generic description. Do not use honorific typography to endorse a belief or
  confer unsupported status. Do not add unexplained honorifics to personal names.
* Italics use paired apostrophes, never Markdown asterisks. Use italics for foreign
  terms, words discussed as words, and book/movie/paper titles. Do not italicize
  an entire quotation merely because it is quoted. Keep surrounding sentence
  punctuation outside italics unless it belongs to the italicized title/phrase.
* Scientific binomials have an initial capital on the genus and lowercase species
  epithet, both italic: ''Homo sapiens''. Keep rank indicators, formulae, unit
  symbols and mathematical operators in their appropriate notation.
* Use source-supported romanization when needed without reversing name order or
  guessing pronunciation. Keep original-script forms accurate when supplied.

== Malagasy elision apostrophes ==
Use no space before the single elision apostrophe and one space after it:
* amin'ny → amin' ny
* an'Andriamanitra → an' Andriamanitra
* amin'izao → amin' izao
* tamin'ny → tamin' ny
* ho an'ny → ho an' ny

These are writing conventions for newly composed Malagasy, including captions
and translated link labels. Preserve already correct spacing. Do not confuse
single elision apostrophes with MediaWiki's ''italics'' or '''bold''' delimiters.
Do not change O'Connor, foreign contractions, names, original titles, direct
quotations, citation metadata, filenames, URLs, IDs, template parameter names,
code or mathematical expressions. Do not perform a raw global substitution.

== Acronyms, abbreviations, and agencies ==
Keep established foreign acronyms and abbreviations when useful, preserving
their letters and conventional punctuation. At first mention write the acronym
followed by a Malagasy translation/expansion in parentheses, even if familiar:
WHO (Fikambanana Iraisam-pirenena momba ny Fahasalamana).
Repeat the explanation only when a standalone caption/table needs it.

Do not invent an acronym from a translated name or import English plural endings.
Explain rather than abbreviate when a shortened form would confuse. Standard
unit/scientific symbols are notation, not prose acronyms needing a repeated gloss.

Foreign agency/institution names may remain in their original language and word
order. Accompany the full name with an accurate Malagasy translation in
parentheses. Italicize the full retained foreign-language phrase; keep the
Malagasy gloss and standalone acronym roman. A descriptive translation is not an
assertion that the organization officially uses that Malagasy name. Never invent
the expansion, institutional status or mandate from initials alone.

== Personal-name order ==
Preserve the original/culturally established order for all names. Translation
does not authorize mechanically moving a final word to the front or applying
Western given-name-first order.
* Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese names retain original order, including
  their romanized forms. Preserve documented individual naming choices rather
  than guessing an order from nationality alone.
* Malagasy names use surname first and given names last when those components
  are verified. This specific local convention is the exception to preserving a
  source's Westernized order in newly written Malagasy prose.
* Do not invent a family name, split a mononym or compound name, treat a pen name
  as an automatically decomposable legal name, or infer a surname from position.
  Retain the evidenced form and record uncertainty when structure is unknown.
* Direct quotations, original titles and citation author metadata preserve the
  source's exact names and ordering. Do not rewrite a bibliography to match
  narrative name order; keep separate author fields semantically accurate.
* Proper personal/place names are not italicized solely because they are foreign.
  Do not translate the components of a personal name.

== Titles of books, films, and papers ==
In narrative mentions, italicize book titles, movie/film titles, and paper or
research-article titles: ''L'Étranger'' and ''On the Electrodynamics of Moving
Bodies'' illustrate markup, not verified translations. Preserve the actual
title's spelling, punctuation, language and internal word order.

Italic paper titles are an explicit local override: the English guide normally
uses quotation marks for papers and other short works. Do not invent a published
Malagasy title; an explanatory translation may follow in parentheses and must
not be misrepresented as an official edition. Keep citation title fields literal
and let verified citation rendering supply typography; do not double-wrap titles
already formatted by a template. A verbatim quotation retains its source text.

== Quotations, citations, and attribution ==
* Keep direct quotations faithful in wording, names, order and meaning. Identify
  the speaker/writer and attach the supporting reference. Mark genuine omissions
  or editorial insertions transparently; never omit a qualification to change a
  quotation's message. Do not silently correct or sanitize source titles.
* Clearly label Malagasy translations of quotations; they are translations, not
  original Malagasy utterances. Preserve controversial wording and force of the
  source without presenting the speaker's judgment as Wikipedia's own voice.
* Do not rewrite words-to-watch occurrences inside original quotations, titles,
  or citation metadata. Faithful reproduction does not waive relevance, copyright,
  reliable sourcing, contextual accuracy or living-person protections.
* Quote selectively; long quotation and close copying are not substitutes for
  original translation/exposition. Do not use scare quotes to imply disbelief.
* Preserve citation-to-claim placement, named reference definitions/reuses/groups,
  authors, titles, dates, pages, URLs, DOI and ISBN. Place reference tags adjacent
  to the supported clause/sentence, normally after punctuation, and provide a
  matching native references renderer for each group.
* Preserve source URLs as data. Do not visit them or claim to have read them
  unless the user explicitly requested that research. Dictionary definitions
  inform translation but do not establish an article's factual claims.

== Punctuation, dates, quantities, and grammar ==
* Use consistent readable punctuation and a single interword space. Distinguish
  apostrophes, quotation marks, hyphens, en dashes for ranges, and mathematical
  minus signs. Never change these characters inside identifiers or URLs.
* Avoid ambiguous slashes and and/or constructions; state whether alternatives,
  combinations, ratios or a sequence are intended. Keep parentheses balanced.
  Do not add rhetorical exclamation marks or double sentence-ending punctuation.
* Adapt grammar, verbal voice and tense to Malagasy while preserving historical
  versus present claims. Do not transfer English possessive endings, English
  collective-noun agreement or English contraction bans to Malagasy elisions.
* Prefer source-supported explicit dates to recently/currently/today. Date relative
  expressions inside quotations by identifying the quotation's context, not by
  rewriting its words. Avoid unqualified northern-hemisphere seasonal assumptions.
* Use consistent unambiguous Malagasy dates; preserve exact source dates in
  quotations/citation metadata. Clarify time zone/calendar where relevant.
* Preserve quantities, uncertainty, significant figures, proportions, units,
  coordinates, currency and time-dependent exchange rates. Never convert using
  an invented rate or change precision to make prose look neater.
* Prefer SI units where suitable, retaining necessary source/specialist units and
  verified equivalences. Use standard unit symbols without invented plural forms.
  Keep values and symbols together with supported nonbreaking spacing where
  appropriate. Use proper math markup without corrupting formula/code syntax.

== Geography, media, lists, tables, and accessibility ==
* Use verified Malagasy place names; country spellings use the cached
  Sokajy:Firenena evidence prescribed in SKILL.md. Preserve historical context
  rather than replacing a former political entity with an anachronistic modern
  one. Names do not establish sovereignty or territorial claims.
* Keep Commons filenames, licenses, orientation and scientific image information
  accurate. Translate captions/alt text; do not infer an identity from appearance
  or fetch external images to verify it. Avoid left/right/above/below references
  whose meaning disappears on mobile or with a screen reader.
* Use succinct captions with consistent sentence punctuation and the same name,
  apostrophe, title and foreign-term conventions as body text.
* Use prose when it is clearer than a list. Use MediaWiki lists and consistent
  grammatical structure; number a list only when sequence/numbering matters.
  Do not insert blank lines that accidentally split a single wiki list.
* Use semantic wikitable headers and captions, not tables for visual page layout.
  Do not rely on color alone, text-only images, forced tiny fonts, or hidden/
  collapsed essential information. Inspect the preview offline without loading
  external resources.
* Link useful concepts to correct local topics, not every repeated common word.
  Do not add misleading links or links/footnotes inside section headings. Put
  selective external links in the appropriate appendix, not as inline substitutes
  for citations; preserving a link does not authorize opening it.
* Prefer simple native wikitext to elaborate HTML/CSS and unverified templates.
  No Markdown, live sandbox categories, mainspace metadata edits, or style bots.

== Wording review and edition gate ==
Read words-to-watch.wiki in full. Its lists are contextual warnings, not banned
tokens. Check the same rhetorical effects in Malagasy, not just English spelling.
Do not remove meaningful uncertainty, legal allegations, or established technical
terminology merely to avoid a listed word.

Before publication, inspect the raw draft and offline preview against this manual.
Record apostrophe spacing, acronym/agency glosses, foreign/title italics, verified
name order, quotation/citation exceptions, source fidelity and neutral wording in
notes.wiki. Set existing fluency/terminology/neutrality/citations review gates true
only after those checks. Automated structural lint is not a language-style proof.
Unresolved material identity or meaning stops autonomous publication; do not ask
questions, invent evidence, or relax conflict/network guards to finish the task.
